jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:
About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

About the Role

We are  seeking a strategic, analytical, and business-savvy Finance Manager to partner closely with Engineering, Product, and our leadership teams to drive financial planning, investment strategy, and operational rigor across the business, with a primary focus on R&D. This role will report to the Director of Strategic Finance and partner with cross-functional leaders to drive financial planning, analysis, forecasting, and strategic decision support. You will play a key role in informing how Armada  allocates  resources and invests in innovation.

Location.  This role is remote-based on the continental US.

What You'll Do

Cross-Functional Partnership

- Act as a trusted finance partner to Engineering, Product, and other business teams

- Collaborate with Accounting on month-end close, accruals, and relevant accounting considerations (e.g., capitalization policies)

- Partner with broader teams (GTM, RevOps, Strategic Finance) to ensure alignment across company plans

Financial Strategy & Planning

- Own financial planning for key functions, with a primary focus on R&D, including budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning

- Partner with Engineering and Product leaders to translate technical roadmaps into financial plans

- Develop and track key metrics (e.g., cost efficiency, headcount productivity)

Investment Strategy & Decision Support

- Evaluate new product initiatives, infrastructure investments, and key business opportunities through detailed financial models and business cases

- Support prioritization of resources across competing initiatives

- Conduct scenario analysis to inform trade-offs between growth, cost, and operational efficiency

Budgeting, Forecasting & Variance Analysis

- Lead budgeting cycles and monthly/quarterly forecast updates for supported functions

- Analyze variances and provide actionable insights to improve cost discipline and predictability

- Partner with business leaders to track performance against financial targets

Process Improvement & Scaling

- Build scalable processes, reporting frameworks, and dashboards to support financial visibility and decision-making

- Improve visibility into spend, hiring, and investment performance

- Drive automation and tooling enhancements across FP&A systems

You’re a Great Fit If You’re

- A  strategic thinker  who can connect technical investments to financial outcomes

- A  hands-on builder  who thrives in ambiguity and creates structure where none exists

- A  strong partner  who can influence without authority and collaborate with technical teams

- A  detail-oriented operator  who can balance precision with speed in a fast-paced environment

- A  self-starter  with a bias for action and ownership

Qualifications

- 5+ years of experience  in FP&A, strategic finance, investment banking, or related roles

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related field;  MBA  or  CPA/CFA  preferred.

- Experience supporting Engineering, Product, R&D, or other technical/business functions preferred

- Strong financial modeling skills (scenario modeling, investment analysis, headcount planning)

- Experience with budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis in a high-growth environment

- Familiarity with software development cost capitalization and related accounting concepts is a plus

- Experience with financial systems (e.g., NetSuite, Pigment, or similar) and data tools

- Advanced Excel proficiency required

Compensation & Benefits

For U.S. Based candidates: To ensure fairness and transparency, the starting  base salary range for this role for candidates in the U.S. are listed, varying based on location experience, skills, and qualifications.  In addition to base salary, this role will also be offered equity and subsidized benefits (details available upon request) .

- Tier 2 (most U.S. metro areas): $121,120 – $154,400

- Tier 3 (other cities): $115,070 - $143,830

Final compensation will be determined by experience, scope, and level, and may vary from the posted range.

- Thrive in a fast-paced environment. You're energized by an entrepreneurial spirit, capable of working quickly, and excited to contribute to a growing company

About the Role

Armada is building a world-class experiential engine, and we’re hiring a Senior Events Operations Manager to run the logistical, technical, and operational foundation behind our global events portfolio.

This role is the day-to-day operator of our events machine, ensuring every program is planned, resourced, documented, and executed with precision across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC. You’ll support executive-level experiences and collaborate closely with events leadership to uphold Armada’s quality bar and ensure programs scale without sacrificing consistency or craft. This role reports directly to the VP of Experiential Marketing and will support across the entire events function.

This is a hands-on, detail-driven, high-ownership role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments and loves turning ambitious ideas into flawlessly run experiences.

Location. This role is remote-based on the continental US.

What You'll Own (Key Responsibilities)

Event Planning & Operational Delivery

- Manage end-to-end operations for third-party conferences, owned experiences, field programs, executive engagements, and internal events.

- Build detailed workback plans, run-of-show documents, staffing plans, production schedules, and contingency plans.

- Oversee registration, attendee communications, F&B, AV, production, transportation, security, and on-site execution.

- Support executive and VIP logistics, which may include travel coordination, briefing materials, green rooms, rehearsals, handlers, and on-site movement, ensuring these experiences meet Armada’s bar for polish and precision.

- Serve as a calm, decisive on-site lead who anticipates issues, resolves them quickly, and protects the guest and executive experience.

Systems, Tools & Portfolio Management

- Build and maintain the operational systems that keep the global portfolio running: intake, briefs, approval workflows, calendars, templates, checklists, and service standards.

- Maintain a single source of truth for event dates, owners, budgets, milestones, executive participation, content needs, and cross-functional dependencies.

- Create scalable processes that ensure consistency across regions while allowing for local adaptation.

- Partner with Marketing Operations to improve event technology, registration systems, lead capture, data hygiene, integrations, and reporting workflows.

- Ensure systems and standards reflect Armada’s experiential expectations and support the broader experiential strategy.

Budget, Vendor & Risk Management

- Own budget tracking, purchase orders, invoices, accruals, reconciliations, and forecasting in partnership with Finance and program owners.

- Lead vendor sourcing and management across agencies, venues, production, audiovisual, fabrication, hospitality, transportation, gifting, and staffing.

- Support contract negotiations, scopes of work, change orders, payment schedules, insurance, permits, and compliance.

- Track inventory, assets, signage, collateral, and shipping logistics to reduce waste and improve reuse.

- Maintain risk, safety, and contingency standards for global events, escalating decisions at the right time.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Measurement

- Partner with Field Marketing, Corporate Marketing, Sales, Executive Operations, Communications, Product Marketing, People, Finance, Legal, and Procurement to deliver aligned programs.

- Collaborate across the entire Events team to ensure operational delivery supports experiential strategy, executive programs, and global consistency.

- Run clear planning cadences, document decisions, surface risks early, and ensure stakeholders understand ownership, deadlines, and next steps.

- Ensure attendee and engagement data is accurate, timely, and connected to the right systems to support pre-event targeting and post-event follow-up.

- Create post-event recaps that capture budget performance, attendance, engagement, operational learnings, and recommendations for continuous improvement.

What You'll Bring

- 8+ years in event operations, experiential production, or event marketing in a fast-paced B2B environment.

- Proven experience managing complex events end-to-end, including executive programs, conferences, field events, internal meetings, and multi-vendor productions.

- Exceptional project management skills with mastery of timelines, budgets, logistics, documentation, and cross-functional coordination.

- Experience managing agencies and vendors, including scopes of work, contracts, production schedules, invoices, and on-site teams.

- Strong financial discipline and comfort owning detailed budget tracking, forecasting, reconciliation, and procurement workflows.

- Clear, proactive communication style and the judgment to know when to solve independently and when to escalate.

- Ability to stay composed under pressure, shift priorities quickly, and maintain a high bar for detail and guest experience.

- Willingness to travel frequently, including internationally, and work early mornings, evenings, and weekends during event cycles.

Nice to Have

- Experience supporting a global event portfolio across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC.

- Familiarity with event platforms, project management tools, CRM/marketing automation systems, and lead capture integrations.

- Experience producing executive briefing centers, customer advisory boards, sales kickoffs, or large-scale flagship events.

- Background in AI, enterprise technology, infrastructure, or energy.

Why This Role Matters

You’ll build the operational foundation that allows Armada’s experiential portfolio to scale with consistency, efficiency, and excellence. Your work will make every program more predictable, more measurable, and more aligned — giving teams and executives confidence that the details are covered and the experience will deliver.

If you love being the operational force behind exceptional experiences, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Sales Strategy & Operations  Manager to own the go-to-market operating cadence for Armada's global sales organization. This role sits within the Revenue Operations team, reporting to the Director, Sales Operations. This role will serve as a key business partner to Sales Leadership, Finance, Deal Desk, and members of the larger RevOps team, ensuring that our sales organization is optimized for scale, efficiency, and predictable growth across our suite of offerings. It serves as the operational backbone for territory and capacity planning, forecasting, pipeline management, and sales performance reporting across our hardware and software portfolio.

The role carries two mandates. The first is the recurring operating rhythm of the business: forecast management, pipeline inspection, territory design and calibration, quota allocation, and the reporting sales leadership runs the business on. The second is transition support as Armada's business units evolve, including planning for evolving or new lines of business and the territory, quota, and compensation that accompanies it.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who wants ownership of key planning workstreams rather than a narrow analytical lane. The ideal candidate is analytically rigorous, thrives in ambiguity, and drives to decisions quickly. You'll join at a pivotal moment, helping build the operating model that scales Armada's sales organization as it brings edge AI infrastructure to customers around the world.

Location. This role is remote-based on the continental US.

What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)

- Partner with sales leadership on regional GTM strategies, providing analysis and recommendations that inform planning and execution

- Support monthly and quarterly business reviews, translating performance data into clear narratives and recommended actions

- Maintain and refine the reporting structure and format sales leadership depends on, including dashboards and recurring deliverables, and recommend definitions of core revenue metrics

- Own the forecast operating rhythm for business unit(s): call preparation, roll-up, commit and category hygiene, and forecast accuracy tracking over time

- Drive pipeline hygiene and the inspection cadence across regions and business units

- Build capacity, headcount and ramp models that size the sales organization against revenue targets

- Design, build and calibrate territory structure in partnership with sales leadership, and allocate quota against approved coverage models

- Maintain account plans and target account definitions in partnership with regional leaders

- Own go-to-market roster management, ensuring joiners, movers and leavers are reflected in payee records, plan assignment and quota allocation

- Partner on segmentation and coverage model design, building the analysis and options that inform coverage decisions

- Develop compensation scenarios and market benchmarking to support plan design

- Administer the sales compensation platform, including plan configuration, period close and payout validation

- Support business unit evolution and creation, including territory and quota re-cuts, compensation plan migration, roster splits, and data and systems separation inputs

- Apply AI tools and automation in support of GTM strategy, and to accelerate recurring analysis and reporting

- Partner with RevOps, Accounting and Finance, People, and Engineering teams with clear ownership boundaries across each

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's Degree required; a Master's Degree may substitute for two years of experience

- 8+ years of experience in sales strategy, sales operations, revenue operations or an equivalent analytical function; consulting, banking and corporate strategy backgrounds welcome

- Demonstrated ownership of territory design, quota allocation, capacity modeling and forecast management

- Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, including modeling, pivot tables and formula-driven analysis

- Working knowledge of Salesforce or a comparable CRM

- Ability to translate complex, ambiguous analysis into concise narratives for senior leaders, and to influence and persuade key partners outside your own function

- Comfort operating with limited structure, and a builder's instinct for establishing process where none exists

- Demonstrated discretion handling compensation and other sensitive data

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience supporting multi-vertical, multi-geography sales teams that sell both hardware and software

- Experience supporting complex, multiparty sales motions to critical heavy industrial or defense customers

- Hands-on experience with a sales compensation platform such as CaptivateIQ, Xactly or Spiff

- Experience supporting a business unit creation or separation

- Familiarity with BI tooling such as Tableau, Looker or Sigma, and SQL proficiency

- Proficiency using AI tools as part of a daily workflow rather than experimentally

- Prior experience in a public sector, defense or other regulated sales environment

What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

Job Title: IT Hardware Procurement Manager (AI Infrastructure)
Location: India(remote)/Dubai

Role Overview

As the IT Hardware Procurement Manager, you will be the strategic architect of our global AI infrastructure supply chain. You will lead the end-to-end sourcing for high-performance compute (HPC) and sovereign AI cloud platforms. This role requires a rare blend of deep technical fluency in NVIDIA architecture and aggressive commercial acumen to ensure supply continuity in a volatile global semiconductor market.

Core Responsibilities

- Strategic Sourcing & Vendor Ecosystem: Identify, vet, and manage Tier 1/2 OEMs and regional distributors for high-density servers, network gear, and cabling. Build a resilient multi-vendor strategy to eliminate single points of failure.

- Commercial Leadership: Drive end-to-end contract lifecycles, including Master Purchase Agreements (MPAs), Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and complex warranty/support negotiations.

- Technical Risk & Inventory Management: Monitor global semiconductor trends to mitigate long-lead-time risks. Support Solution Engineering by ensuring "just-in-time" inventory of mission-critical hardware (GPUs, NICs, Switches).

- Cross-Functional Roadmap Alignment: Partner with Systems Engineering and Architecture teams to translate technical specs into scalable, multi-year procurement roadmaps.

- System Integration Support: Oversee the procurement and delivery of integrated components, including NVIDIA Grace CPUs , NVLink , InfiniBand , and ConnectX-8

- Sovereign AI & Compliance: Architect procurement workflows that satisfy stringent security, data residency, and national compliance requirements for Sovereign AI cloud deployments.

Qualifications

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical STEM field.

- HPC Expertise: 5+ years of experience in high-performance computing (HPC) or hyperscale datacenter procurement environments.

- Systems Knowledge: Foundational understanding of the hardware-software stack, including operating systems, device drivers, and firmware versioning.

- Strategic Communication: Ability to bridge the gap between technical engineering requirements and executive-level financial/commercial constraints.

Preferred Qualifications

- Global Logistics: Proven experience navigating regional distributor landscapes in APAC and EMEA .

- Modular Infrastructure: Experience with rack-level integration for modular or Edge datacenter deployments.

- AI Workload Optimization: Practical knowledge of how hardware specifications impact specific AI workloads (LLM training vs. low-latency inference).

jobs.title: Vice President, People & Talent
jobs.description:
About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Armada is hiring a Vice President, People and Talent to own the full People stack and build the infrastructure a globally distributed company needs to scale. This is end-to-end ownership: Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, People Operations, and Compliance, with real depth expected in global mobility, entity and employer-of-record management, and compensation design.

Roughly two thirds of the role is that operating stack. The remaining third is employee experience and culture: workspace and physical environment strategy, onboarding, and building learning and development programming from the ground up.

This is not an execution-only seat. Our executive team expects the People function to carry a point of view on how talent decisions drive the business, and to bring that perspective into leadership conversations rather than waiting to be handed requirements. You will define the strategy and own the execution.

You are building, not inheriting. Programs, policies, systems, and team headcount are yours to stand up.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

Talent Acquisition and Workforce Planning

- Own global recruiting strategy across technical and non-technical functions, and stay close enough to the work to personally run a critical search if needed

- Implement structured hiring processes that raise talent density and hold hiring managers accountable

- Move time-to-hire and quality-of-hire against defined baselines

- Partner with Finance to align headcount planning, workforce modeling, and geographic expansion with budget forecasting

Total Rewards and Compensation

- Own compensation philosophy and band architecture, mapped to Armada levels and defensible against a named benchmarking source

- Own equity strategy at the pre-IPO stage: new hire grants, refresh and evergreen programs, 409A cadence, and the exception process

- Run the annual compensation and merit cycle in partnership with Finance, including geographic differentials across owned entities and employer-of-record markets

- Design and manage global benefits programs and renewals, balancing cost, competitiveness, and local requirements

- Prepare executive compensation recommendations and materials for the CEO, [the Board compensation committee,] and Finance

People Operations, Compliance, and Systems

- Design and scale a People Operations framework that holds global consistency while allowing for local nuance

- Own the compliance posture across every operating jurisdiction, partnering with Legal on employment law, immigration, and risk mitigation

- Oversee payroll operations, vendor management, audit readiness, documentation standards, and internal controls

- Own the People technology stack (HRIS, ATS, payroll, performance, analytics) and the data governance that makes workforce reporting trustworthy

International Expansion, Entities, and Mobility

- Own entity strategy: decide where Armada uses an employer of record and where it stands up a local entity, and run the conversion when the answer changes

- Manage employment, labor compliance, and employee relations across international jurisdictions

- Own global mobility, relocation, and immigration programs in partnership with Legal

Employee Experience, Workspaces, and Culture

- Define workspace and physical environment strategy across offices, remote environments, and field deployments

- Own onboarding end to end, so a new hire in any location starts productive and stays connected

- Partner with Finance and Operations on real estate strategy, cost management, and vendor selection

- Set standards for workplace experience, safety, and compliance across all locations

Learning, Development, and Manager Capability

- Build learning and development programming from the ground up, starting with what the business needs most rather than a catalog

- Partner with the executive team on organizational design, leveling frameworks, and job architecture

- Implement performance management that gives managers a clear, usable standard rather than a process to survive

- Build manager capability through explicit leadership expectations, development, and coaching

WHAT YOU WILL BRING

- Proven experience running the full People stack end to end: Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, People Operations, and Workspaces

- Expertise in global mobility, employer-of-record versus entity management, and compensation design

- Built and scaled a People function through high growth, in the range of 250 to 1,000+ employees, standing up programs, policies, and team headcount from scratch rather than inheriting an established function

- Took a company through IPO or another exit, and can articulate how that outcome shaped your compensation philosophy

- Managed entity setup and employee management across international jurisdictions

- Experience with workspace and physical environment strategy, onboarding, and building learning and development programming

- A track record of staying through the build: you have carried companies across multiple phases of growth to an outcome rather than moving on at each inflection point

- Operates as a business partner to the executive team, with a clear point of view on what the People function is for and the judgment to bring it forward unprompted

Nice to Have

- Experience supporting a federal-facing entity, including hiring, badging, and the compliance requirements specific to a cleared workforce

- Hands-on Middle East experience: employer-of-record arrangements versus local entity setup, and managing employees across the UAE, KSA, and Bahrain labor and compliance landscapes

Compensation & Benefits

For U.S. Based candidates: To ensure fairness and transparency, the starting  base salary range for this role for candidates in the U.S. are listed, varying based on location experience, skills, and qualifications.  In addition to base salary, this role will also be offered equity and subsidized benefits (details available upon request) .

Final compensation will be determined by experience, scope, and level, and may vary from the posted range.

Benefits

- Competitive base salary and equity

- Medical, dental, and vision (subsidized cost)

- Health savings accounts (HSA), flexible spending accounts (FSA), and dependent care FSAs (DCFSA)

- Retirement plan options, including 401(k) and Roth 401(k)

- Unlimited paid time off (PTO)

- 14 paid company holidays per year

- Thrive in a fast-paced environment. You're energized by an entrepreneurial spirit, capable of working quickly, and excited to contribute to a growing company

- Highly organized and results-driven. Strong prioritization skills and a dedicated work ethic are essential for you
